stem: A hospital has excess readmissions for conditions included in the CMS Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP). Which nursing quality-improvement strategy most directly aligns with the program's stated purpose?

options.A: Strengthen discharge communication and care coordination and actively engage clients and caregivers in post-discharge plans
options.B: Limit improvement work to elective surgical scheduling because HRRP does not include medical conditions
options.C: Focus on changing billing codes without addressing discharge communication or care coordination
options.D: Reduce follow-up communication after discharge so clients return only if symptoms become severe

rationale: CMS describes HRRP as a Medicare value-based purchasing program that encourages hospitals to improve communication and care coordination, better engage patients and caregivers in discharge plans, and reduce avoidable readmissions. HRRP includes both medical conditions and procedures. Changing billing documentation alone does not address the program's care-quality goal, and reducing follow-up communication conflicts with coordinated transitional care. Therefore A is the best answer.
educational_objective: Use coordinated discharge communication and patient/caregiver engagement as quality-improvement strategies that align with CMS HRRP efforts to reduce avoidable readmissions.
source_version_date: CMS page last modified 2026-03-10; FY 2026 program confirmed in CMS-1833-F
source_locator: Sections 'What is the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program?' and 'Why is the Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program important?': Medicare value-based purchasing program encouraging improved communication and care coordination to engage patients/caregivers in discharge plans and reduce avoidable readmissions; FY 2026 IPPS final-rule fact sheet — HRRP reduces payments to hospitals with excess readmissions and links payment to quality of hospital care
source_claim_supported: HRRP links payment to hospital quality and encourages communication, care coordination, and patient/caregiver engagement in discharge planning to reduce avoidable readmissions.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care — Performance Improvement (Quality Improvement), printed p.22 / PDF p.26: participate in performance-improvement projects and quality-improvement processes; evaluate impact on client care and resource use. Management of Care — Continuity of Care: perform safe discharge procedures and follow up unresolved client-care issues
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — Performance Improvement / readmission reduction and discharge coordination
correction_summary: Converted a program-purpose recall question into an applied nursing quality-improvement item. Anchored the correct action to CMS's current HRRP language on communication, care coordination, patient/caregiver engagement, and discharge planning.
audit_findings: A directly matches CMS's current stated HRRP strategy. B is false because HRRP includes several medical conditions as well as procedures. C addresses coding rather than care-quality improvement, and D undermines post-discharge coordination. The item does not imply that every readmission is preventable or that nursing alone determines HRRP payment. One best answer remains with direct NCSBN Performance Improvement/Continuity mapping. Independent second pass found no unresolved conflict.
